title: How the UK tax and welfare system works

groups.title: Taxes on earnings and income
groups.intro: What comes off pay and other income before it reaches the person.

items.name: Income Tax (England, Wales and Northern Ireland)
items.summary: Tax on earnings, pensions and most other income above a tax-free Personal Allowance, charged in bands. Scotland sets its own rates on earnings and pensions (next entry); dividends and savings are taxed the same across the UK.
items.who: Anyone with taxable income above the allowance.

parts.label: Personal Allowance taper
parts.value: £1 lost for every £2 of adjusted net income over £100,000; gone completely at £125,140
parts.note: Worked out from this: between £100,000 and £125,140 each extra £1 earned is taxed at 40% and also costs 50p of allowance, an effective 60% rate.

parts.label: Marriage Allowance
parts.value: transfer £1,260 of Personal Allowance to a spouse or civil partner, saving them up to £252

interactions: The 60% effective rate between £100,000 and £125,140 sits on top of National Insurance (2%), and for some people the High Income Child Benefit Charge, student loan repayments and the loss of Tax-Free Childcare (all at £100,000 for the childcare).
Pension contributions made through the employer or with tax relief can bring adjusted net income back down below a threshold.

items.name: Income Tax (Scotland)
items.summary: Scottish residents pay Scottish rates and bands on earnings, pensions and most other non-savings, non-dividend income; the Personal Allowance is the same.
items.who: People resident in Scotland.
items.admin: HMRC collects it for the Scottish Government

items.name: National Insurance: employees (Class 1)
items.summary: Paid by employees on weekly (or monthly) earnings between two thresholds, at a low rate above the upper one. It also builds entitlement to the State Pension and some benefits.
items.who: Employees aged 16 to State Pension age.

parts.label: Nothing on earnings up to
parts.note: Between £129 and £242 a week nothing is paid but the year counts towards benefits.

parts.label: Main rate (category A)
parts.value: 8% on earnings from £242.01 to £967 a week (£50,270 a year)

parts.label: Who stops paying
parts.value: at State Pension age for employees
parts.note: Employees stop paying Class 1 when they reach State Pension age.

items.name: National Insurance: employers (Class 1 secondary)
items.summary: Paid by the employer on each employee's earnings above a low threshold, not deducted from pay; on benefits in kind the employer pays Class 1A.
items.who: Employers.

parts.label: Starts above
parts.value: £96 a week (£5,000 a year) for most employees

parts.label: Upper secondary threshold
parts.value: £967 a week for under-21s, apprentices under 25 and veterans: nothing is paid between the secondary and upper thresholds for them

interactions: Economists generally expect much of this to fall on wages and profits rather than on the employer alone: a costing has to say what it assumes (see the costing specification).

items.name: National Insurance: self-employed (Classes 2 and 4)
items.summary: Class 4 is a percentage of profits between two thresholds; Class 2 is no longer compulsory.
items.who: Self-employed people.

parts.label: Class 2
parts.value: no payment needed from £7,105 of profits (counts as paid); £3.65 a week if paid voluntarily below that

items.name: Student loan repayments
items.summary: Not a tax, but collected through payroll like one: a share of income above a threshold, in addition to tax and National Insurance, until the loan is repaid or written off.
items.who: Anyone with a student loan in repayment.

parts.label: Plan 1
verify: 9% of your income over the threshold

parts.label: Postgraduate Loan
verify: 6% of your income over the threshold

interactions: Repayments run alongside income tax and National Insurance, so a Plan 2 borrower in the basic-rate band faces 20% + 8% + 9% = 37% on each extra £1 (worked out from the rules shown here).

items.name: High Income Child Benefit Charge
items.summary: A tax charge that claws back Child Benefit from households where one person has a high income.
items.who: Anyone with Child Benefit in the household, where the higher earner has income over £60,000.

parts.label: Rate
parts.value: 1% of the Child Benefit for every £200 over £60,000
verify: 1% of your Child Benefit for every £200

interactions: Between £60,000 and £80,000 the clawback behaves like an extra marginal rate on top of 40% income tax and 2% National Insurance; the size depends on the number of children.

items.name: Tax relief on pensions
items.summary: Contributions to a private pension get tax relief, up to limits.
items.who: Anyone paying into a private pension.

parts.label: Relief limit
parts.value: contributions up to 100% of earnings in a year get relief

parts.label: Relief at source
parts.value: the provider claims 20%; higher-rate payers claim the rest through tax

items.name: ISAs
items.summary: Savings and investment accounts whose returns are tax-free.
items.who: Adults saving.

parts.label: Annual limit
parts.value: £20,000 across all ISAs in the year

parts.label: Lifetime ISA
parts.value: up to £4,000 a year within the limit

items.name: Tax on dividends
items.summary: Dividends above an allowance are taxed at rates that depend on the income tax band they fall in.
items.who: Shareholders outside ISAs and pensions.

items.name: Value Added Tax
items.summary: A tax on most goods and services sold by VAT-registered businesses, which pass it on to the buyer.
items.who: Buyers of goods and services; collected by VAT-registered businesses.

parts.label: Zero rate
parts.value: 0% (the sale is covered by VAT, but nothing is charged)

items.name: Fuel Duty
items.summary: A tax per litre on petrol, diesel and other road fuels, charged before VAT. The rates are set in pounds and pence per litre (or per kilogram for gases) rather than as a percentage of price.
items.who: Fuel suppliers, passed on to motorists and businesses.

parts.label: Unleaded petrol, diesel and bioethanol or biodiesel
Marked gas oil (red diesel) and kerosene for excepted machines
parts.value: £0.1018 a litre, temporarily cut to £0.0648 from 15 June 2026 to 30 June 2027

items.name: Alcohol Duty
items.summary: A tax per litre of pure alcohol, in bands by strength, with lower rates for draught products.
items.who: Producers and importers, passed on in prices.

parts.label: Draught (3.5% to under 8.5%: beer, wine, spirits)

items.name: Tobacco Products Duty
items.summary: Tobacco is taxed per thousand cigarettes or per kilogram, with cigarettes also charged a share of the retail price and a minimum amount. Rates from 1 October 2026.
items.who: Manufacturers and importers, passed on in prices.

parts.label: Cigarettes
parts.value: the higher of 16.5% of the retail price plus £394.09 per 1,000, or £518.75 per 1,000 (the minimum excise tax)

interactions: Behaviour matters a great deal for tobacco: much of a rise in duty can be lost as people smoke less or buy illicit tobacco, which is why costing specifications treat it as a high-uncertainty measure.

items.name: Air Passenger Duty
items.summary: A tax per passenger on flights from UK airports, by distance band and class of travel. Rates from 1 April 2026.
items.who: Airline passengers.

parts.label: Band A (up to 2,000 miles): reduced / standard / higher

items.name: Insurance Premium Tax
items.summary: A tax on general insurance premiums, with a higher rate for travel insurance, some appliance insurance and some vehicle insurance.
items.who: Buyers of general insurance.

groups.title: Taxes on wealth, property and gains
groups.intro: Charged on gains, on property bought, and on estates.

items.name: Capital Gains Tax
items.summary: A tax on the profit from selling assets such as shares and second homes.
items.who: People and trustees selling assets at a gain.

parts.label: Basic rate band for the calculation
parts.value: £37,700: gains within it (after taxable income) are at 18%

items.name: Inheritance Tax
items.summary: A tax on estates (and some lifetime gifts) above a threshold.
items.who: Estates above the threshold.

parts.label: Rate
parts.value: 40% on the value above the threshold

parts.label: Charity
parts.value: 36% if 10% or more of the net estate goes to charity

parts.label: Gifts
parts.value: £3,000 a year exempt; gifts within seven years of death may be taxed

items.name: Stamp Duty Land Tax (England and Northern Ireland)
items.summary: A tax on buying property, charged in bands on the part of the price in each band.
items.who: Buyers of property in England and Northern Ireland (Scotland and Wales have their own taxes).

parts.label: First-time buyers
parts.value: nothing up to £300,000, then 5% to £500,000; no relief on homes over £500,000

groups.title: Local and devolved property taxes
groups.intro: Set by councils and the devolved governments, not by the UK Parliament alone.

items.name: Council Tax
items.summary: A tax on homes in England, Scotland and Wales, set by the local council within the national rules and charged by property band. The band charges are set locally each year; the national rules give discounts.
items.who: The people living in a home.

parts.label: Single person
parts.value: 25% off the bill if you live alone (and pay Council Tax)

parts.label: Everyone in the household 'disregarded'
parts.value: 50% off the bill (for example if everyone is a full-time student)

parts.label: Average Band D, England, 2026-27
parts.value: £2,392 (up £111, or 4.9%, on 2025-26), including adult social care and parish precepts

parts.label: Average Band D by type of area
parts.value: London £2,068; metropolitan areas £2,409; unitary areas £2,490; shire areas £2,452

parts.label: Limit on rises
parts.value: a referendum is needed above the principles: 5% for authorities with adult social care duties (up to 2% for adult social care and 3% for other spending), with higher limits for a few named councils
verify: 2% for expenditure on adult social care

interactions: Many councils also run a Council Tax Reduction scheme for people on low incomes; its rules are set locally.

items.name: Business rates
items.summary: A tax on non-domestic property in England: the property's rateable value multiplied by a multiplier set each year, with reliefs.
items.who: Occupiers of business premises.

parts.label: How the bill is worked out
parts.value: rateable value × the multiplier (standard or small business)

parts.label: Small business rate relief
parts.value: may be available if the business uses one property in England with a rateable value under £15,000

parts.label: Retail, hospitality and leisure
parts.value: relief replaced by two new rate multipliers
verify: Retail, hospitality and leisure rate relief has been replaced with two new rate multipliers

items.name: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland)
items.summary: Scotland's tax on buying property, in place of Stamp Duty Land Tax: charged in bands on the part of the price in each band.
items.who: Buyers of residential property in Scotland.

items.name: Corporation Tax
items.summary: A tax on company profits, with a lower rate for small companies and marginal relief in between.
items.who: Companies.

parts.label: Between the two
parts.value: marginal relief: an effective rate between 19% and 25% on profits from £50,000 to £250,000

items.name: Employment Allowance
items.summary: A relief that cuts an employer's annual Class 1 National Insurance bill.
items.who: Eligible employers.

parts.label: Amount
parts.value: up to £10,500 off employers' Class 1 National Insurance each tax year

parts.label: Who can claim
parts.value: from April 2025, employers with Class 1 liabilities over £100,000 can claim too

items.name: Apprenticeship Levy
items.summary: A charge on large employers' pay bills, which funds apprenticeships.
items.who: Large employers.

parts.label: Who pays
parts.value: employers with an annual pay bill over £3 million (including connected companies)

items.name: Capital allowances
items.summary: Tax relief for businesses on spending on plant and machinery, in place of depreciation.
items.who: Businesses buying plant and machinery.

parts.label: Annual investment allowance
parts.value: up to £1 million a year of qualifying spending

parts.label: Full expensing
parts.value: 100% first-year relief on qualifying plant and machinery from 1 April 2023

parts.label: 40% first-year allowance
parts.value: for qualifying plant and machinery bought after 1 January 2026

parts.label: Writing down allowances
parts.value: for spending that does not qualify for another allowance, and any value left over

groups.title: Welfare: working-age and families
groups.intro: Amounts for 2026-27 (and, where different, last year's) read from the DWP's published rates.

items.name: Universal Credit
items.summary: The main means-tested benefit for people of working age on a low income, in or out of work. It combines the support that used to be in several benefits and is reduced as earnings rise.
items.who: Working-age people and families on a low income.

parts.label: Standard allowance: couple, one or both 25 or over
Child element: first child (born before 6 April 2017)
Child element: first child born from 6 April 2017, and other children
Limited capability for work and work-related activity (new claims)
parts.note: The amount for people who claimed before 2026, and for severe conditions and terminal illness, is higher: see the DWP table.

parts.label: Childcare: one child (up to 85% of costs)
Taper
parts.value: payment falls by 55p for every £1 earned above the work allowance
parts.note: Earnings are taxed first, so the 55p applies to take-home pay: see the marginal rates explorer for the combined effect with tax and National Insurance.

parts.label: Savings between £6,000 and the limit count as income of

interactions: Because UC is reduced by 55p for each £1 of earnings above the work allowance, it adds to the marginal rate of tax and National Insurance: the combined effect is shown in the marginal rates explorer.
The benefit cap limits the total of UC and other benefits a household can receive (see Benefit cap).
Student loan repayments and the High Income Child Benefit Charge are separate and do not reduce UC.

items.name: Benefit cap
items.summary: A limit on the total benefit income of a working-age household. It is waived for households with earnings of £881 a month or more after tax and National Insurance, and for several disability and caring groups.
items.who: Working-age households not exempt.

parts.label: Couples, or single parents (Greater London), a year
Single adults, no children (Greater London), a year
Couples, or single parents (rest of Great Britain), a year
Single adults, no children (rest of Great Britain), a year
Earnings exemption
parts.value: £881 a month combined, after tax and National Insurance (from 1 April 2026)

items.name: Child Benefit
items.summary: A payment for each child, not means-tested, but clawed back through tax from households where someone has a high income (the High Income Child Benefit Charge, above).
items.who: Anyone responsible for a child.
interactions: The High Income Child Benefit Charge claws it back between £60,000 and £80,000 of individual income.

items.name: Tax-Free Childcare
items.summary: The government tops up money paid into a childcare account.
items.who: Working parents.

parts.label: Top-up
parts.value: £2 for every £8 paid in, up to £2,000 a year per child (£4,000 if the child is disabled)

parts.label: Income limit
parts.value: no support if either partner's expected adjusted net income is over £100,000

items.name: Jobseeker's Allowance and Employment and Support Allowance
items.summary: Older, 'legacy' benefits that Universal Credit is replacing; the new-style versions are paid on National Insurance contributions.
items.who: Jobseekers and people with limited capability for work.

parts.label: ESA (contributory and new style): 25 or over
ESA (contributory and new style): work-related activity component
ESA (contributory and new style): support component

items.name: Statutory sick, maternity and other family pay
items.summary: Paid by employers (and reclaimed in part), at a flat rate or a share of earnings.
items.who: Employees (and some self-employed people for Maternity Allowance).

parts.label: Statutory Sick Pay: standard rate (or 80% of average earnings if lower)

items.name: Housing Benefit and Local Housing Allowance
items.summary: Help with rent for people who have not moved to Universal Credit, mainly pensioners and some supported housing. For private renters the amount is capped by the Local Housing Allowance, set from local private rents.
items.who: Tenants of working age in supported housing and pensioners; most working-age renters get the housing element of Universal Credit instead.

parts.label: Single or lone parent, reached State Pension age on or after 1 April 2021
Couple, both reached State Pension age on or after 1 April 2021
Local Housing Allowance
parts.value: set by the area's private rents (a Broad Rental Market Area) and the bedrooms the household needs
parts.note: Area rates are looked up on GOV.UK by postcode, so they are not copied here.

items.name: Warm Home Discount
items.summary: A one-off discount on an electricity bill for people on certain benefits or low incomes.
items.who: People on Pension Credit or in a low-income household.

items.name: Free school meals (England)
items.summary: Free lunches for children in families on certain benefits.
items.who: Children of families on these benefits.

parts.label: Universal Credit
parts.value: household income of £7,400 a year or less after tax, not counting benefits (for claims from 1 April 2018)

parts.label: Other qualifying benefits
parts.value: income-related Employment and Support Allowance; the guaranteed element of Pension Credit; some asylum support

items.name: Scottish Child Payment
items.summary: A payment from the Scottish Government to low-income families with children under 16.
items.who: Low-income families in Scotland.

parts.label: Amount
parts.value: £28.20 a week for each eligible child, paid every four weeks (£112.80)

parts.label: Number of children
parts.value: no limit on the number of children in a family who can get it
verify: no limit on the number of children

groups.title: Welfare: disability, health and caring
groups.intro: Not means-tested, apart from the additions in other benefits.

items.name: Personal Independence Payment
items.summary: Help with the extra costs of a long-term illness or disability, in two parts; people of working age.
items.who: People with a long-term condition, assessed on how it affects daily life.

items.name: Attendance Allowance
items.summary: The equivalent for people over State Pension age who need care.
items.who: Over State Pension age, with care needs.

items.name: Carer's Allowance
items.summary: For people who spend at least 35 hours a week caring for someone getting a disability benefit, with an earnings limit.
items.who: Carers.

groups.title: Welfare: pensioners
groups.intro: State Pension and the top-ups for pensioners on low incomes.

items.name: State Pension
items.summary: The new State Pension is paid to people reaching State Pension age since April 2016; the old basic pension to those before.
items.who: People over State Pension age with enough National Insurance years.

parts.label: Old basic State Pension (category A or B)

items.name: Pension Credit
items.summary: Tops a pensioner's income up to a minimum level (the Guarantee Credit), with a small extra for savings (Savings Credit).
items.who: People over the Pension Credit age on a low income.

parts.label: Guarantee Credit: couple
parts.value: tops joint weekly income up to £363.25

parts.label: Savings
parts.value: the first £10,000 is ignored; each £500 above it counts as £1 a week of income

interactions: Getting Pension Credit opens up other help (for example Warm Home Discount and the Winter Fuel Payment in full).

items.name: Winter Fuel Payment
items.summary: A payment to pensioners for heating costs, which HMRC takes back through tax from people with a higher income.
items.who: Pensioners.

parts.label: Clawback
parts.value: taken back if the person's total income is over £35,000

gaps: Wales' Land Transaction Tax and other Welsh Government taxes: the Welsh Government's site refuses automated access (its robots.txt blocks bots), so it is not read here.
Scottish benefits other than the Scottish Child Payment (for example Adult Disability Payment, Carer Support Payment, Best Start Grant): the amounts are not on pages that could be read reliably yet.

Soft Drinks Industry Levy, Plastic Packaging Tax, Climate Change Levy and vehicle tax rates: the GOV.UK pages found carry historic or partial rate tables, so a current figure could not be checked against them.
Bank levy and Digital Services Tax: no GOV.UK rates page was found to read them from.

Council Tax by individual council (the national averages are included; each council's own band charges are in the Government's Table 10 spreadsheet), Local Housing Allowance rates (looked up by area) and the yearly business rates multipliers.

Child Tax Credit and Working Tax Credit (closed; replaced by Universal Credit) and the detail of who qualifies for each payment: this page gives rates, thresholds and tapers, not every eligibility rule.
